derivations.claim: By [A4], $\eta_{ab}$ is constant in this inertial chart, so every derivative $\partial_c\eta_{ab}$ vanishes. The connection formula in [F1] therefore gives $\Gamma^a{}_{bc}=0$, so $\nabla_aF^{ab}=\partial_aF^{ab}$ in this chart. The exterior equation in [A1] is expressed by the partial-derivative formula in [F5].

If two of $\lambda,\mu,
u$ coincide, the cyclic sum in (TM2) vanishes: for example, when $\lambda=\mu$, it is $\partial_\lambda(F_{\lambda
u}+F_{
u\lambda})+\partial_
u F_{\lambda\lambda}=0$ by [F5]; the cases $\lambda=
u$ and $\mu=
u$ have the same cancellation after writing out the three terms. For distinct indices, swapping the first two gives $S_{\mu\lambda
u}=\partial_\mu F_{\lambda
u}+\partial_\lambda F_{
u\mu}+\partial_
u F_{\mu\lambda}=-S_{\lambda\mu
u}$ by $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$; swapping the last two or first and last gives the same sign change by the same termwise substitution. Since transpositions generate all permutations, every distinct-index instance is, up to sign, one of the four triples $(1,2,3)$, $(0,1,2)$, $(0,2,3)$, $(0,3,1)$.
Lower the current index with $\eta$: $j_0=\eta_{00}j^0=-c\rho$ and $j_i=J_i$ by [F1] and [F3]. This determines every component needed for $f^\nu=F^{\nu\lambda}j_\lambda$.

For $\nu=0$, alternation gives $F^{00}=0$ and [F2] gives $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$. Thus $\partial_\mu F^{\mu0}=-c^{-1}\sum_i\partial_iE_i=-(\operatorname{div}E)/c$, while $-\mu_0j^0=-\mu_0c\rho$ by [F3]. Since $c>0$, the $\nu=0$ equation of (TM1) is equivalent to $\operatorname{div}E=\mu_0c^2\rho=\rho/\varepsilon_0$.

For each $i\in\{1,2,3\}$, $\partial_\mu F^{\mu i}=\partial_0F^{0i}+\partial_jF^{ji}=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i+\epsilon_{jik}\partial_jB_k=c^{-2}\partial_tE_i-(\operatorname{curl}B)_i$. Here $F^{ji}=\epsilon_{jik}B_k=-\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ and $\epsilon_{jik}=-\epsilon_{ijk}$; the right side of (TM1) is $-\mu_0J_i$. Rearranging this equality gives exactly the $i$th component of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$, and the rearrangement is reversible.

The $(1,2,3)$ instance of (TM2) is $\partial_1F_{23}+\partial_2F_{31}+\partial_3F_{12}=\sum_i\partial_iB_i=\operatorname{div}B$, since $\epsilon_{123}=\epsilon_{231}=\epsilon_{312}=1$ in [F2] and [F4]. Therefore this independent homogeneous equation is equivalent to $\operatorname{div}B=0$.

Antisymmetry makes the $\lambda=0$ term of $f^0$ vanish, and [F2] gives $f^0=F^{0i}j_i=\sum_i(E_i/c)J_i=(J\cdot E)/c$. Under the additional matter-model hypothesis of [A3], this is its adopted electromagnetic power density divided by $c$.

For each spatial index, $f^i=F^{i0}j_0+F^{ij}j_j=(-E_i/c)(-c\rho)+\epsilon_{ijk}B_kJ_j=\rho E_i+\epsilon_{ijk}J_jB_k=\rho E_i+(J\times B)_i$ by [F2] and [F6]. Under the additional matter-model hypothesis of [A3], this is its adopted electromagnetic spatial force density.

For a cyclic ordering $(i,j,k)$ of $(1,2,3)$, the $(0,i,j)$ instance is $\partial_0F_{ij}+\partial_iF_{j0}+\partial_jF_{0i}=c^{-1}\bigl(\partial_tB_k+\partial_iE_j-\partial_jE_i\bigr)=c^{-1}\bigl(\partial_tB_k+(\operatorname{curl}E)_k\bigr)$. This uses $F_{ij}=B_k$, $F_{j0}=E_j/c$, $F_{0i}=-E_i/c$, and $\epsilon_{kij}=1$ for this cyclic ordering. The three cyclic choices give the three components of $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$, with each equation reversible. By the alternating property in step 1.2, these and step 2.3 account for every instance of (TM2).

The units are consistent: $[\rho E]=\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}}\,\mathrm{V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, $[J\times B]=\mathrm{A\,m^{-2}}\,\mathrm{T}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, and $[J\cdot E]=\mathrm{W\,m^{-3}}$, so $[f^0]=[J\cdot E]/c=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$. Thus the tensor contraction has the units of force density; its force/power interpretation additionally requires the matter-model hypothesis of [A3], with SI normalization fixed by [F3].

Steps 2.1 and 2.2 identify the four sourced equations in (TM1) exactly with Gauss's electric law and the Ampère–Maxwell law; steps 2.3 and 3.1 identify the independent homogeneous components exactly with Gauss's magnetic law and Faraday's law, while step 1.2 handles all repeated indices and reduces the remaining triples to those four. Thus (TM1) and (TM2) hold if and only if all four vector equations in the Statement hold. These are precisely the smooth vacuum equations adopted in [A2]; no second-derivative, boundary, weak-field, or singular-source claim has entered.

The first-order component equivalence and contraction identities use the stated regularity and flat dictionary [A4]; on the smooth subclass they identify the curved postulate [A1] with [A2]. Only the physical force/power interpretation uses the additional matter-model hypothesis [A3]. The curved continuation in [A1] remains an adopted physical model assumption; this component check does not infer an Einstein solution for nonzero $F$, a global inertial chart on a curved manifold, or empirical validity of any postulate.

supplier_excerpts.exact_statement: Now let $n=3$ and let $F:U\to\mathbb R^3$ be $C^1$ on an open $U\subseteq\mathbb R^3$. Following [[def-cross-product-in-r3]], write the three coordinates of a point and of a vector as $x,y,z$ rather than $0,1,2$, so that $F=(F_x,F_y,F_z)$ means $F=(F_0,F_1,F_2)$ and $\partial_x,\partial_y,\partial_z$ are $\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2$. With that naming, the **curl** of $F$ is $\operatorname{curl}F:=(\partial_yF_z-\partial_zF_y,\ \partial_zF_x-\partial_xF_z,\ \partial_xF_y-\partial_yF_x)$, a map $U\to\mathbb R^3$ each of whose coordinates is continuous on $U$. In this naming the divergence reads $\operatorname{div}F=\partial_xF_x+\partial_yF_y+\partial_zF_z$.

derivations.claim: The vector $n=\partial_0$ has $\eta(n,n)=-1$ and is future-directed, so it is an observer. From $F_{10}=E_0/c$, $F_{20}=F_{30}=0$, the definition in [F1] gives $E=(E_0,0,0)$. By [F3], $\star_\eta F=(E_0/c)dx^2\wedge dx^3+B_0dx^0\wedge dx^1$, so $-({\star_\eta F})_{i0}$ has components $(B_0,0,0)$; hence $B=(B_0,0,0)$.

Both coefficients are constant and each coordinate one-form is closed, so the coordinate exterior derivative formula in [F2] gives $dF=0$. Every component $F^{ab}$ is constant, and the flat connection vanishes; therefore $\nabla_aF^{ab}=\partial_aF^{ab}=0=-\mu_0j^b$ for each $b$, since $j=0$. Both adopted Maxwell equations in [A1] hold everywhere on this prescribed background.
